assessment.security_status: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu prudce eskaluje po bleskové vojenské operaci Húthiů podél jemenského pobřeží Rudého moře a úspěšných údronech a raketových útocích na saúdská ropná zařízení. Útoky v Hormuzském průlivu a rostoucí riziko zapojení regionálních sil (Pakistán, Egypt) posouvají konflikt do fáze přímého ohrožení globální energetické infrastruktury.

recommendations.reason: Dlouhodobé odklonění tras mimo Rudé moře a Hormuzský průliv udržuje spotové sazby vysoko a generuje nadstandardní marže přepravců navzdory rizikům.

recommendations.sector: Obranný průmysl (např. RTX, Lockheed Martin, BAE Systems)
recommendations.reason: Intenzivní využívání protiraketové obrany v Zálivu a přímé útoky na Saúdskou Arábii a Jemen zajišťují vysokou poptávku po vojenském vybavení a systémech PVO.

recommendations.sector: Ropa a Plyn (např. Shell, BP, Chevron)
recommendations.reason: Zastavení klíčového saúdského ropovodu po dronovém útoku a výpadky produkce o miliony barelů denně tlačí ceny ropy prudce vzhůru.

recommendations.sector: Evropský Spotřební sektor & Autoprůmysl (např. Volvo, BMW)
recommendations.reason: Přetrvávající logistické výpadky, dražší energie a potíže s dodávkami komponent z Asie negativně dopadnou na marže a poptávku.

recommendations.sector: Pražská burza: ČEZ, Komerční banka, Erste Group
recommendations.reason: Domácí banky zůstávají stabilní, zatímco ČEZ těží z vysokých cen energií, ale celkový globální geopolitický šok brzdí výraznější růst.

assessment.forecast: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující extrémní volatilitu cen ropy, růst nákladů na námořní pojištění a zvýšenou diplomatickou i vojenskou aktivitu koaličních sil v Rudém moři.
assessment.forecast_review: Předchozí předpověď se potvrdila, protože eskalace konfliktu v Jemenu a útoky na energetickou infrastrukturu vedly k dalšímu růstu cen ropy a udržení vysoké volatility.

articles.title: Battle of Chile director Patricio Guzmán dies aged 85
articles.summary:
Passionate documentary maker won international acclaim for unsparing but poetic films exploring the impact of the Pinochet regime in Chile

Patricio Guzmán, the film-maker who chronicled Chile’s bloody 1970s political strife and its subsequent social and political turmoil in films such as The Battle of Chile and Nostalgia for the Light, has died aged 85. According to Chilean news outlet Emol, Guzmán died on Tuesday in Paris after a cardiorespiratory arrest.

Guzmán’s chief preoccupation throughout his career was the carnage unleashed by Augusto Pinochet’s coup in 1973 against Salvador Allende, Chile’s elected president. He later told the Guardian: “I’m a film-maker who was very marked by the ways of the dictator. It has remained with me for ever. I cannot leave it behind.” However, he resisted the idea that he was an activist, political film-maker, adding: “I’m not a sociologist. Neither am I a politician. I make films that are metaphorical and poetic; I interpret reality through my own personal way of looking.”

articles.title: Thursday briefing: Yemen’s war continues to threaten oil supplies– but what about its people?
articles.summary:
In today’s newsletter: The Houthi advance along the Red Sea coast raised fears for global trade and energy supplies, while more than 100,000 Yemenis have been displaced by the fighting

Good morning. The lightning advance of Houthi militants along the west coast of Yemen over the past week has prompted fears of a spiralling conflict in the region and a new oil supply crisis.

For families living in the Middle East’s poorest country, the most significant fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthis and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces in years is a crisis upon a catastrophe, with escalating civilian casualties and at least 100,000 displaced in recent days.

articles.title: Fighting in Yemen pushing health system to ‘collapse’, says WHO chief
articles.summary:
Fighting in Yemen pushing health system to ‘collapse’, says WHO chief

Escalating tensions in Yemen are “pushing an already fragile health system closer to collapse”, director general of the World Health Organisation Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned on Thursday.

“Nearly 20 million people need health assistance, while outbreaks of cholera, measles, polio and dengue, as well as malnutrition, threaten more lives,” Ghebreyesus wrote on X, adding “peace is the best medicine”.

Escalating violence in #Yemen is causing more casualties and displacement, pushing an already fragile health system closer to collapse.

articles.title: EU condemns alleged Houthi strikes on Mecca
articles.summary:
EU condemns alleged Houthi strikes on Mecca

The EU voiced its "full solidarity" with Saudi Arabia on Thursday as it condemned recent strikes on the kingdom by Yemen's Houthis, including an attempted attack on Islam's holy city of Mecca, which the Houthis have denied carrying out.

"We urge the Houthis to cease all military action," EU Foreign Affairs spokesperson Anouar El Anouni said in a statement, adding that "the targeting of civilians and civilian infrastructure is unacceptable."

Reporting by AFP

articles.title: Yemeni government says Houthis suffering heavy blows
articles.summary:
Yemeni government says Houthis suffering heavy blows

The Yemeni government’s army said on Thursday that it targeted Houthi supplies and military positions in Taiz and Mocha in southwestern Yemen.

Chairman of the Yemeni Presidential Leadership Council, Rashad al-Alimi, also said Houthi forces are suffering heavy blows on the fronts in Taiz, Marib, Lahj, al-Jawf, Hajjah, al-Bayda and al-Dhale.

In a meeting with the French ambassador to Yemen, al-Alimi called the Houthis' gains temporary, according to Yemen's Saba news agency, adding that “the state and its armed forces are fully capable of regaining the initiative on the West Coast”. 

This comes after the Houthis seized territories on Yemen’s Red Sea coast in a lightning advance, while Saudi-backed government forces fought to regain control of southwestern Yemen.

articles.title: Pakistan says time has come to implement Mecca defence pact
articles.summary:
Pakistan says time has come to implement Mecca defence pact

Pakistan’s defence minister has said the time has come to implement the Mecca defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkey as Houthi attacks on the kingdom intensify.

Speaking to Geo News on Wednesday, Khawaja Asif said Pakistan remained committed to defending Saudi Arabia and the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, adding that Islamabad had a duty to protect them even without the agreement.

“Makkah Agreement applies to us, and we will fulfil our duty,” said Asif without elaborating on what Pakistan may do.

Houthi officials have denied targeting the holy city.

"Our operations target its [Saudi] oil facilities and military bases, which are far removed from the sacred sites," Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said.
